What came first, viral threats or conditions that enable viral mutations?  That lovely picture of a pasture-based dairy system, of a farm averaging around 50-200 cows, isn’t the problem.  Not when the majority of dairy products originate from large commercial farms containing anywhere from 500 to several thousand cows, packed into dense, immunocompromising environments, and fed anything but fresh grass.

Regulatory changes are the fix here, not bandages in the form of a few bucks thrown at the US dairy industry that currently generates ~$65B in annual revenue.  Leadership is required such as taken in California with Proposition 12, Farm Animal Confinement. https://t.co/gtbCdurnwv

With $65B on the line, that’s a battle and a half, in parallel to our growing viral threats and associated risks of pandemic costs that are many times greater.  Until then, speaking of bandages, we better have two important healthcare remedies in place:

1. Prevention of viral replication in hosts (vaccines; leadership in support of health-positive lifestyle changes)

2. Treating viral sepsis, the dysregulated immune response to viral infection leading to long-term poor health if not death (therapeutics aimed at Controlling Inflammation such as #Gohibic).
